audit_findings.title: Owner earnings may omit required working-capital reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 operating cash flow was $2.581 million and free cash flow was $1.330 million, versus the $14.5 million OE anchor; the recurring normalized working-capital requirement is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A normalized increase in receivables and inventory required to support sales should reduce OE before the anchor is projected and capitalized.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash flows provided by operations decreased by $7,609,846, or 74.7%, during the year ended December 31, 2025, to $2,580,794, as compared to $10,190,640 during the same period in Fiscal 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation reconstruction omits changes in working capital, while 2025 required substantial cash for receivables and inventory. Some of that cash was recovered in first-half 2026, so the full 2025 gap is not demonstrated to be recurring. Nevertheless, even a fraction of the $13.17 million gap between the anchor and 2025 free cash flow could materially reduce all scenarios.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct annual OE including changes in operating receivables, inventory, prepaids, payables and operating liabilities; normalize those changes over a full commodity cycle and rerun every scenario with the resulting OE anchor.

audit_findings.title: The bridge may add operating cash as though it were excess
audit_findings.magnitude: $43.442 million added to the bridge, equal to 17.6% of the $247 million base equity value and $1.67 per share; required operating cash is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash required for procurement, settlement delays, taxes, debt maturities or ordinary liquidity is operating capital and must not be added as a separate non-operating asset.
audit_findings.evidence: The impact on working capital is having to pay more to procure inventory, and the delayed conversion of accounts receivable from refiners.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge treats the entire June 2026 cash balance as distributable. The balance was partly produced by a $13.24 million release of receivables and inventory during first-half 2026, but the business still faces commodity-driven procurement and settlement requirements and $7.589 million of current notes payable. The record does not establish that all $43.442 million is excess, and the bridge amount is large enough to change the valuation materially.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a monthly liquidity analysis covering procurement, seasonal inventory, refiner-settlement delays, taxes, lease payments and 2026 debt maturities; rerun the bridge using only the cash demonstrably above the resulting minimum requirement.

audit_findings.title: A commodity-assisted peak year is being capitalized as the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 consolidated operating income increased $9.950 million to $18.109 million and consumer operating income increased $6.532 million to $6.678 million; the required normalization adjustment is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An above-cycle 2025 OE anchor raises every forecast-year cash flow and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The change was primarily attributed to higher transaction volumes, which were supported by the upward movement in gold and silver prices throughout the year.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing directly attributes higher consumer volumes to rising gold and silver prices. First-half 2026 results show continued strength, but management also described first-quarter precious-metals prices and selling activity as exceptional and reported moderation toward typical activity in the second quarter. Thus persistence is not disproved, but ordinary-cycle OE has not been established; because the entire $172 million to $240 million operating valuation is anchored to $14.5 million, normalization is material.
audit_findings.action: Build a consumer-segment volume and margin normalization using multiple years and ordinary metal-price, supply-flow and refiner-capacity conditions; replace only the anchor with normalized OE and rerun bear, base and bull values.

audit_findings.title: Customer and receivable concentration threatens anchor durability
audit_findings.magnitude: Two customers represented 54.9% of 2025 sales and 68.3% of year-end A/R; two customers represented 50.8% of first-half 2026 sales but 0.0% of June 2026 A/R
audit_findings.mechanism: Loss, repricing or slower settlement by concentrated outlets could reduce future OE or increase working-capital needs.
audit_findings.evidence: For the year ended December 31, 2025, two customers aggregated 54.9 % of our sales and represented 68.3 % of our accounts receivable balance.
audit_findings.explanation: The concentration is demonstrated, but a valuation error is not. The year-end receivable was subsequently collected, and the company describes these customers as short-duration precious-metals outlets with alternative channels. The record does not disclose their gross-profit contribution, contractual dependence or the economics of switching outlets, so value materiality remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain customer-level gross profit, settlement history, contract and termination terms, credit exposure, and comparable pricing and capacity from alternative outlets; stress OE and working capital for loss or repricing of each customer.

audit_findings.title: A capitalized contract-acquisition cash cost may be missing from OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $573,502 combined 2025 prepaid-expense movement cited in the filing; the contract-acquisition component and recurring annual amount are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring cash paid to obtain or renew contracts reduces OE even if capitalized in prepaid assets rather than reported as capital expenditure.
audit_findings.evidence: Prepaid expenses: a $573,502 net increase primarily attributed to our commercial segment, resulting from incurring costs in Fiscal 2025 to obtain a contract and from a reduction in prepaid freight associated with our ITAD revenue share settlements in Fiscal 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that cash was spent to obtain a contract, but combines that amount with a change in prepaid freight. It therefore does not establish the contract cost, its amortization period, renewal frequency or whether it is recurring. The possible OE omission is real, but the record cannot establish its valuation magnitude.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the prepaid-asset roll-forward and underlying contract, separate acquisition costs from freight, determine amortization and renewal terms, and rerun OE with a normalized recurring contract-acquisition deduction.

audit_findings.title: A one-time employee-retention credit may remain in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: At most $96,480 pre-tax and approximately $75,254 after tax, or 0.52% of the $14.5 million anchor; approximately $0.04 per share in the base case if fully capitalized
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring credit left in other income would increase 2025 OE and every projected cash flow.
audit_findings.evidence: The segment also received an employee retention credit in Fiscal 2025, while Fiscal 2024 included the proportionate share of income from a settlement for repairs related to our corporate headquarters.
audit_findings.explanation: Consumer other income was $352,295, of which disclosed dividend and interest income totaled $255,815, leaving only $96,480 for the credit and any other items. Even treating that entire residual as the credit, applying the 22% effective tax rate and capitalizing it at the base-case operating-value-to-anchor multiple changes base value by only about $1.06 million, or $0.04 per share versus $9.52 per share.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the credit amount and its treatment in the OE reconstruction; remove its after-tax contribution for precision, but no conclusion-changing rerun is required unless the ledger identifies a materially larger amount.
